notes: Prepared on 2026-11-18. No production data edited. Eight full EvidenceRecord additions; no inferred reciprocal routes and no intermediate nodes.
All connection geometries have two regional endpoints and routeKind/basis schematic. Site coordinates are deliberately generalized and must not be described as exact artifact findspots.
Numerical cal BP conversions use 1950 minus cal BP, matching the repository convention; originals are retained. Explicit BCE dates use astronomical map years.
The California shell recipient is Santa Rita village in Pleasanton, an inland East Bay locality, not a coastal shellmound.

Source access note: the original CaliforniaPrehistory Rick PDF URL currently returns404; the coauthor-hosted deschutesmeridian copy was read through the browser index. Its table text is rotated but numerical entries agree with narrative discussion for SMI-172; SMI-528 is explicitly listed as1480–1120calBP.

Priority audit order: (1) explicit Chaco Pacific/Gulf distinction; (2) early California material movement; (3) a primary-sourced Atlantic pottery connection; (4) BCE/earlyHolocene river-region breadth. All four regions still have further recoverable material evidence.
Audited data/trade-0-1200-expansion-records.json, data/trade-0-1200-corrections.json, data/trade-0-1200-scenes.json, and docs/trade-coverage-audit.md. No production files changed.
All eight connections are source-to-find schematics. No proposed road, intermediate place, sailing schedule, modern ethnic attribution, or continuous annual trade was inserted.

Early and later Alca contexts are separate from the existing ninth-century Quilcapampa record. Caribbean records and San Lorenzo/Copán early phases fill families absent from the reviewed 38-observation set.
History kind exchange follows the existing broad overlay schema; prose explicitly identifies cases where procurement/personal mobility versus exchange is unresolved.
User's later Inca/Aztec request will be a separate handoff at actual imperial dates, not backdated into these windows.
Eight new connections; no production edits. Three Teouma source connections describe one archaeological exchange network, not independently dated systems.
Coordinates are rounded locality or region anchors. Lines indicate material provenance, not nautical tracks.
Use disjoint history.windows for the Australian stone connection; do not fill its evidence gap.
Nagsabaran is held as migration-versus-exchange context. A founding settlement alone does not establish trade.
Seven source-to-find connections span BCE and CE evidence. Existing trade expansion and baseline were checked for these endpoints and materials; no duplicate connection was found.
Regional source anchors are deliberately broad; the two glass source points are not identified manufacturing workshops. No intermediary sites are inserted merely to make a plausible path.
Palmyra is a lower-confidence catalogue-based addition; the single approximate year preserves the supplied date rather than inventing a century-long trade interval.
Berenike's -49 to50 interval is an explicit editorial half-century rendering of late first-century BCE / early first-century CE; original wording remains authoritative.
No production data, tests, build outputs or branches changed.
Existing trade overlays audited before additions: r9v-inca-atacama-road-exchange is unplaced road activity; r11v-cusco-obsidian-continuity concerns 600–1000, not the imperial flows added here.
All dates are later than 1200. No Aztec/Inca network is backdated to the pre-1200 priority period.
No artifacts are generated from missing historical routes; all geometry is explicitly schematic.
